meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 2.40%, its biggest one-day gain in seven months; foreign investors bought ₹14,975 crore (provisional); the Nasdaq fell 5.52%.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Fri 6 Nov: NIFTY 50 up 2.40% for a sixth gain as the Nasdaq falls 5.52%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 2.40% to 24,536.60 and the Sensex 2.60% to 79,310.01 on Thursday, a sixth straight gain and the largest one-day rise in seven months (Upstox News).
Nearly every sector index rose, led by Nifty Auto (up 4.14%), while media and energy fell (Upstox News, HDFC Sky). Bajaj Finance, up 7.65%, led the NIFTY 50.
Foreign investors bought a net ₹14,975 crore and domestic institutions sold ₹10,445 crore (provisional). Business Standard said the foreign figure was the highest since February 2021.

Overnight, the Nasdaq fell 5.52%, its worst day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 4.36% as chip and AI shares were sold; Brent crude settled 3.88% higher at $98.29 after tanker attacks near Hormuz (Reuters).

drivers.title: Foreign flows
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹14,975 crore on 5 Nov (provisional), after ₹7,284 crore on 4 Nov. Foreign flows feed into large-cap share prices and the rupee; provisional figures can be revised when final data is published.

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent touched an intraday low of about $93.50 a barrel on 5 Nov (Upstox News), then settled 3.88% higher at $98.29 after fresh tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reported. India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee and inflation.

drivers.title: The rupee and bonds
drivers.text: PTI said lower crude and foreign inflows lifted the rupee to 94.41 per dollar. The 10-year government bond yield fell to 7.17%, down 24 basis points so far in November, Business Standard reported. Bond prices rise when yields fall.

drivers.title: Inflation
drivers.text: Retail inflation was 5.54% in September, up from 4.83% in August (Business Today). October's reading is due on 12 Nov, according to MoSPI's release calendar.

global_cues.title: US shares
global_cues.text: The Nasdaq fell 5.52%, its worst day since April 2025, while the S&P 500 lost 4.36% and the Dow 3.44% on 5 Nov as chip and AI shares were sold (Reuters). Sharp US moves reach India through overnight sentiment, foreign flows and the US clients of Indian IT companies.

global_cues.title: US yields and the dollar
global_cues.text: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell about 5 basis points to about 4.84% as investors moved into bonds, and the dollar index was little changed. US yields and the dollar shape foreign flows and the rupee.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: Asian shares fell in early trade on 6 Nov, Reuters reported: the Kospi dropped more than 8%, setting off a trading halt, and the Nikkei was about 6% lower. Asia is the last major cue before the Indian open.

events.title: US jobs report
events.text: Economists polled by Dow Jones expect 59,000 jobs added in October, after 29,000 in September, CNBC reported. US data moves Treasury yields and the dollar.

events.title: US Federal Reserve
events.text: Futures pricing put the chance of a December Fed rate hike at about 66% to 69% on 5 Nov, down from about 83% a day earlier, Kitco News reported.

global.headline: The Nasdaq had its worst day since April 2025 as chip and AI stocks fell; the Bank of England raised rates

source.name: Alliance News via Yahoo Finance UK

global.note: On 5 Nov Hong Kong rose while Seoul and Tokyo fell. Gold held a gain of about 0.6% overseas as US yields fell, and silver slipped about 0.8% (Kitco News).

us.title: The session
us.text: The Nasdaq had its biggest one-day fall since April 2025 on 5 Nov, Reuters reported. Selling in chip and AI stocks spread after Democrats won both houses of Congress, on concern that tighter rules on AI and opposition to data centres could slow the build-out.

us.title: Technology
us.text: The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell more than 12%. Nvidia lost about 9% and Micron and AMD about 17% each; Qualcomm fell 9.5% after reporting its smartphone chip sales.

us.title: Rates
us.text: Treasuries rallied as investors sought safety. Fed officials Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin both hinted that rate hikes remain possible, Reuters reported.

events.title: Democrats win both houses of Congress
events.text: Democrats took control of the Senate and the House in the 3 Nov midterms, and on 5 Nov US markets reacted to the prospect of tighter oversight of AI and data centres (Reuters). The channel to India: US yields and the dollar, which bear on foreign flows.

events.title: Bank of England raises rates
events.text: The Bank of England raised its rate by 0.25 percentage point to 4.00% on 5 Nov, its first increase since August 2023, on an 8 to 1 vote. Governor Andrew Bailey said another rise is likely unless the Middle East conflict is resolved. The channel to India: global rates and bond yields.

events.title: Oil and the Strait of Hormuz
events.text: Brent rose after fresh tanker attacks near Hormuz, and Eurasia Group cut its estimate of the chance of a US and Iran deal to 10% from 20%, Reuters reported. The channel to India: crude prices and the import bill.

events.title: Gold and central banks
events.text: ANZ analysts said central banks bought a net 321 tonnes of gold in the third quarter, the fastest pace since late 2024. The channel to India: international gold prices set domestic gold rates.

highlights.text: Among equity categories, small cap funds took in a net ₹9,038.57 crore in September, mid cap funds ₹7,834.84 crore and flexi cap funds ₹6,701.80 crore. Large cap funds drew ₹859.47 crore, while ELSS funds saw a net outflow of ₹662.14 crore.
Passive funds took in a net ₹11,887 crore: equity ETFs ₹9,960 crore, gold ETFs ₹4,451 crore and silver ETFs ₹1,974 crore.
Folios rose 0.9% to 28.62 crore, from 28.35 crore in August.

nfo_summary.text: Five new fund offers are open on 6 November, according to Cafemutual and Angel One: an energy ETF, a silver ETF, two silver funds of funds (one of them closing on 6 November) and a realty index fund. Each scheme's category, riskometer level and terms are in its scheme information document. This list is reported for information only and is not a recommendation.

regulatory.text: Since 1 November, direct plans are the default option on fund houses' own digital platforms, and investors who choose a regular plan there are told it carries a higher expense ratio. Regular plans remain available.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, a mid cap fund is an open-ended equity scheme that must keep at least 65% of its total assets in the shares of mid cap companies, which SEBI defines as the 101st to 250th listed companies by full market capitalisation. SEBI's circular of 26 February 2026 kept the 65% minimum. These are equity schemes, so their value rises and falls with the share prices of mid-sized companies, and each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: Where a scheme's riskometer is published
paragraphs: Every mutual fund scheme carries a riskometer, a dial that shows the level of risk of the scheme's portfolio, from low to very high.
For a new fund offer, the riskometer appears in the scheme's key information memorandum and scheme information document, which the fund house publishes before the offer opens.
The level describes the portfolio, not the investor, and it can change after launch as the portfolio changes, so the fund house's latest documents carry the current level.
